title: Private upgrades: E2E test plan (upgrade + rollback mechanism)
content:
Owner: Sahana Iyer (CI/integration tests)
Primary contributors: Leila Farouk (QA automation), Rafael Mendes (SRE), Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
Last reviewed with: Vivek Kulkarni (PM), Ethan Park (CP), Irene Choi (Infra), Fatima Noor (on-prem)

Purpose
This doc defines the end-to-end (E2E) test plan for the “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” project. The goal is to validate that the private installer + Helm packaging + platform version gating behave correctly for:
- Standard N-1 -> N upgrades
- Preflight failures (must-block vs warn)
- Backup + restore orchestration (supported backends)
- Deterministic rollback entry points (including partial upgrades)
- Air-gapped/on-prem upgrade bundles (artifact verification)
- Auditability (events emitted + support bundle capture)

Non-goals
- Exhaustive multi-hop upgrades across multiple major versions in the E2E suite (we’ll test only the supported default path: N-1 -> N).
- Performance benchmarking (covered elsewhere; we’ll only check “upgrade doesn’t degrade cluster health” signals).

Definitions
- CP = control plane components (installer-managed services, API/control-plane deployments)
- DP = data plane components (serving runtime, model cache, worker pools)
- “Plan” = staged upgrade plan artifact generated by redwood-private-installer (auditable JSON + summary)
- “Upgrade window” = time-bound execution configured by operator/terraform (relevant for gating + comms, not strictly enforced by tests except for scheduling validations)

Acceptance criteria (E2E suite)
1) Upgrade success path: For each supported environment profile, installer generates plan, passes prechecks, executes CP then DP phases, and ends with healthy postchecks.
2) Rollback success path: If any stage fails after backup completed, rollback command returns system to pre-upgrade version with expected invariants (see Rollback invariants).
3) Precheck behavior correctness: must-block checks prevent execution; warnings are surfaced but allow “--allow-warnings” (or equivalent) behavior where permitted.
4) Artifact integrity (air-gapped): checksum/signature mismatch is detected and produces actionable errors; valid bundles proceed.
5) Auditability: upgrade lifecycle emits audit events with required fields; support bundle contains upgrade plan + last-run logs.
6) Repeatability/idempotency: rerunning an upgrade after transient failure does not produce inconsistent state; rollback is safe to rerun.

Test execution strategy
- PR gating: A smaller “smoke” E2E subset runs on every PR touching installer/charts/platform gating.
- Nightly: Full matrix, including failure injection and air-gapped flow.
- Release gating: Prior to cutting a Private release train build, run full matrix on pinned artifacts for N-1 -> N.

CI jobs (proposed naming + triggers)
Note: exact pipeline implementation may vary (GitHub Actions vs Buildkite). This doc standardizes job names + what they do for reporting.

PR gating jobs (required to merge for relevant paths)
- private-e2e-smoke-vpc-eks
  - Triggers: PRs affecting redwood-private-installer/, redwood-helm-charts/, redwood/ (compat policy), redwood-terraform/
  - Coverage: 1 env profile, happy path upgrade + postchecks
- private-e2e-smoke-precheck-failures
  - Coverage: storage headroom must-block + artifact availability must-block

Nightly jobs
- private-e2e-matrix-vpc
  - Coverage: multi-K8s versions + storage backends (EBS/CSI), upgrade + rollback
- private-e2e-matrix-onprem-airgapped
  - Coverage: kind/k3s (as proxy), NFS/CSI, offline bundle verification, upgrade + rollback
- private-e2e-failure-injection
  - Coverage: DB migration lock timeout, partial Helm rollout, CP connectivity flap

Release gating jobs
- private-e2e-release-candidate
  - Coverage: exact artifacts destined for release (installer version, charts version, CP policy version)
  - Produces: JUnit + summarized upgrade artifacts attached to build

Required fixtures and test harness
Test harness responsibilities
- Provision ephemeral cluster (EKS for VPC tests; kind/k3s for on-prem simulation)
- Deploy baseline Redwood Private version (N-1)
- Seed minimal “customer-like” state:
  - Config objects (auth config, routing policy, model pins)
  - DB entries (org/project records, audit log sink config if applicable)
  - Model cache seed (optional; small artifact to exercise DP cache handling)
- Create/attach storage backend profiles
- Prepare upgrade artifacts:
  - Online mode: charts/images fetched from standard artifact source or mirror endpoint
  - Offline mode: generated bundle with manifest + checksums/signatures

Fixtures (by category)
1) Versions/artifacts
- Baseline release “N-1”: pinned via terraform var or installer flag
- Target release “N”: pinned via terraform var or installer flag
- Compatibility matrix stub/test policy (when running against main branch) to validate enforcement paths

2) Storage backends
- EBS/CSI snapshot capable profile (VPC)
- CSI generic snapshot profile (where supported)
- Logical DB dump fallback profile (for backends without snapshots)
- On-prem-like NFS or hostPath (simulate “no snapshot” constraints; forces logical backups)

3) Identity/networking
- OIDC reachable profile (happy path)
- OIDC unreachable profile (precheck warns or blocks depending on configured auth mode)
- DNS/TLS mismatch profile (must-block)

4) DB migration stressors
- Migration lock timeout simulation (introduce artificial lock via fixture job)
- Slow migration simulation (forces installer to surface progress + timeouts appropriately)

5) Air-gapped bundle
- Valid bundle: correct checksums/signature
- Invalid bundle: corrupted checksum, missing artifact, wrong signature chain

6) Observability/audit
- Audit sink stub (captures emitted events for assertions)
- Support bundle collector stub (verifies inclusion of plan + logs)

Environment matrix
We’ll keep the matrix intentionally small for PR gating and broader for nightly.

PR gating (minimum)
- Env: VPC
- K8s: 1 version (currently 1.29)
- Storage: EBS snapshots
- Auth: OIDC reachable
- Upgrade path: N-1 -> N
- Tests: upgrade happy path + postchecks; one must-block precheck scenario

Nightly (target)
VPC profiles
- K8s: 1.28, 1.29, 1.30 (as supported)
- Storage: EBS snapshots; CSI snapshots (if supported in test cluster)
- Artifact sources: default + mirror endpoint (terraform/pr-1340)

On-prem/air-gapped profiles
- Cluster: kind (fast) + k3s (closer to on-prem behavior)
- Storage: NFS/hostPath (no snapshot) -> forces logical backup path
- Artifact sources: offline bundle only

Scenario catalog
Each scenario includes: setup, steps, assertions, artifacts captured.

S0. Baseline install (sanity)
Setup
- Provision cluster, install Redwood Private N-1.
Steps
- Run installer “install” with standard config.
Assertions
- All CP/DP pods ready; health endpoints OK.
- Installer writes state to expected location.
Artifacts
- install logs, cluster events, helm release list.

S1. Happy path upgrade (N-1 -> N)
Setup
- Start from S0.
Steps
1) Generate upgrade plan.
2) Run prechecks.
3) Run backup orchestration.
4) Execute upgrade plan (CP phase then DP phase).
5) Run postchecks.
Assertions
- Plan generation output is persisted and includes stage ordering CP->DP.
- Prechecks pass (no must-block failures).
- Backup status “complete” with expected snapshot/dump markers.
- CP upgraded and healthy before DP rollout begins (readiness gate verified).
- Post-upgrade: key APIs respond; no crashloops.
Artifacts
- plan.json + summary, precheck report, backup report, helm history, audit events.

S2. Precheck must-block: insufficient storage headroom
Setup
- Constrain PVC/volume free space to below threshold.
Steps
- Run prechecks for upgrade.
Assertions
- Precheck fails with severity MUST_BLOCK and remediation includes “increase PV size / prune logs / expand node disk”.
- Upgrade execution is prevented (no Helm upgrade attempted).
Artifacts
- precheck report, cluster df output.
Notes
- Mirrors real support case pattern (ref: SUP-18577).

S3. Precheck must-block: artifact unavailable / wrong version
Setup
- Configure artifact source to a missing charts version.
Steps
- Generate plan, run prechecks.
Assertions
- Fails with clear error: missing chart/image, identifies exact artifact coordinate.
- No backup started.
Artifacts
- plan generation output + precheck logs.

S4. Precheck warn: OIDC reachability degraded (when auth mode allows)
Setup
- Use auth mode where OIDC is optional (or set “continue with warnings” enabled).
- Block outbound to IdP.
Steps
- Run prechecks.
Assertions
- Precheck is WARNING (not MUST_BLOCK) and includes risk statement.
- Upgrade can proceed only if operator passes “--allow-warnings” (or configured equivalent).
Artifacts
- precheck report, command invocation captured.

S5. Backup path: snapshot-based
Setup
- VPC/EBS profile.
Steps
- Run upgrade with backup enabled.
Assertions
- Snapshot hooks invoked; snapshot IDs recorded.
- Installer marks a restore point tied to plan execution ID.
- If upgrade succeeds, backup is retained per configured retention.
Artifacts
- backup report, snapshot metadata.

S6. Backup path: logical dump fallback
Setup
- On-prem profile with storage backend lacking snapshots.
Steps
- Run upgrade with backup enabled.
Assertions
- Logical backup runs and is encrypted (if configured); output stored in expected location.
- Restore verification step is executed (e.g., checksum/restore dry run) where supported.
Artifacts
- backup logs, dump file metadata, verification report.

S7. Failure injection: DB migration lock timeout -> rollback
Setup
- Induce DB lock so migration hits lock timeout (align with redwood/pr-29210 guardrails).
Steps
1) Start upgrade; allow backup to complete.
2) Trigger migration failure.
3) Invoke rollback command.
Assertions
- Upgrade fails with explicit “migration lock timeout” and points to mitigation.
- Rollback executes defined hooks in reverse ordering.
- Post-rollback: version is N-1, CP/DP healthy.
- No repeated crashloops; installer state shows rollback completed.
Artifacts
- migration logs, rollback logs, post-rollback health report.
Notes
- This is the highest-value regression test (ref: SUP-18421 patterns).

S8. Failure injection: partial Helm rollout (DP) -> rollback
Setup
- Introduce failure in DP rollout (e.g., bad image tag or readiness probe failure) after CP completes.
Steps
- Start upgrade; allow CP to complete; fail DP rollout; invoke rollback.
Assertions
- Rollback returns DP to previous version.
- CP returns to previous version or remains compatible depending on rollback contract (assert against contract; update once final).
- Helm history shows rollback-safe behavior (no stuck hooks).
Artifacts
- helm events, rollout status, rollback artifacts.

S9. Air-gapped: valid bundle upgrade
Setup
- Build offline bundle for N; include manifest, checksums, signature.
Steps
- Run installer upgrade pointing to local bundle.
Assertions
- Bundle verification passes.
- Upgrade succeeds without external network access.
Artifacts
- bundle verification report, plan, upgrade logs.

S10. Air-gapped: invalid bundle verification fails (checksum/signature)
Setup
- Corrupt one artifact or checksum entry.
Steps
- Run prechecks / verification.
Assertions
- Must-block failure with precise identification of failing artifact + expected vs actual checksum.
- No upgrade steps run.
Artifacts
- verification logs.
Notes
- Regression coverage for offline verification work (ref: installer/pr-4871 and SUP-18510 patterns).

S11. Compatibility policy enforcement (unsupported jump)
Setup
- Attempt upgrade from N-2 -> N (or other disallowed path).
Steps
- Generate plan / run gating.
Assertions
- Installer/platform policy blocks with explicit “unsupported upgrade path” and points to supported path.
- Emits audit event for blocked attempt (if implemented).
Artifacts
- policy evaluation output, audit event capture.

S12. Auditability + support bundle contents
Setup
- Enable audit sink stub and support bundle collection.
Steps
- Execute S1 and one failure scenario (S7).
Assertions
- Audit events emitted: upgrade_started, prechecks_passed/failed, backup_completed, upgrade_completed, rollback_invoked, rollback_completed.
- Events include required fields: environment ID, operator identity (where available), from_version/to_version, plan_id, execution_id, timestamps.
- Support bundle includes: plan.json, plan summary, precheck report, backup report, last-run installer logs.
Artifacts
- captured audit events, support bundle index listing.

Rollback invariants (to be asserted in rollback scenarios)
- Control-plane/data-plane versions match expected post-rollback target.
- No pending Helm hooks/jobs left running.
- DB schema is at a compatible version for N-1 (or forward-compatible if contract requires; assert based on migration guardrails decision).
- Installer state machine marks rollback as COMPLETE and idempotent.
- Operator can re-attempt upgrade after remediation.

Observability checks (lightweight)
These are not “performance tests” but do verify the platform is healthy enough to be considered upgraded.
- Error rates during upgrade window: should not exceed threshold for health endpoints (in test, we assert no sustained 5xx for CP health endpoint).
- Migration duration: record metric; assert it is reported and not stuck beyond timeout.
- Upgrade dashboards annotation: if incident-bot or annotations are available in test env, ensure upgrade window annotation is emitted (best-effort; not gating for GA initially).

Data management and cleanup
- Always collect artifacts even on failure (plan, precheck report, logs, helm history, cluster events).
- Ensure teardown deletes clusters and snapshots/dumps in CI to control cost.
- For snapshot tests: tag snapshots with execution_id and TTL.

Flakiness management
- Retry policy only for cluster provisioning steps (not for upgrade correctness).
- For known flaky operations (image pulls in shared runners), prefer pre-pulled images or private mirror in CI.
- Track flakes under INT-3302; when adding retries, require postmortem entry + follow-up to remove.

Open questions / TODO
- Finalize “warnings allowed” UX flag name in installer and update scenarios S4 accordingly.
- Confirm rollback contract for CP version in partial DP rollout failures (S8) once ADR is finalized.
- Decide which K8s versions are officially supported for GA; update nightly matrix.
- Confirm whether support bundle inclusion is mandatory for PR gating or only release gating.

Change log
2025-05-06: Initial draft created (Sahana).
2025-05-22: Added air-gapped scenarios + artifact verification (Fatima feedback).
2025-06-03: Expanded rollback invariants and migration failure injection (Rafael/Connor feedback).
2025-06-18: Added auditability + support bundle assertions (Allison + security review notes).
